w: Sofia takes its name from this church — in 1329 the town of Serdica was renamed after it. Built in the fourth century, the building survived conversion into a mosque under Ottoman rule before being restored as a basilica, and remains one of the oldest churches standing in the city.
s: The church that gave Sofia its name
_facts: Built as a church in the fourth century CE
Converted into a mosque in the 16th century, restored as a basilica in the 19th-20th centuries
One of the oldest churches in Sofia
In 1329 CE the town of Serdica was renamed Sofia after this church

w: Sofia's archaeology collection lives inside a fifteenth-century mosque — construction began in 1451 under grand vizier Veli Mahmud Pasha, finishing in 1494. The building later housed the National Library before the museum moved in, officially opening in 1905 under its old Ottoman dome.
s: Bulgaria's antiquities, under an Ottoman dome
_facts: Occupies the building of the largest and oldest former Ottoman mosque in the city (Koca Mahmut Pasa Camii)
Construction started in 1451 under grand vizier Veli Mahmud Pasha, completed 1494
Established as a separate museum entity in 1893, officially opened 1905
Previously housed the National Library between 1880 and 1893

w: Completed in 1909, this is the largest synagogue in southeastern Europe and the third largest on the continent — built for a Jewish community that has since largely emigrated to Israel. Only fifty or sixty worshippers now gather beneath its dome, one of just two active synagogues left in the country.
s: SE Europe's largest synagogue, built in 1909
_facts: Completed in 1909
Largest synagogue in Southeastern Europe, third-largest in Europe
One of only two active synagogues remaining in Bulgaria
Regular services draw only 50-60 worshippers due to Jewish emigration to Israel

w: Built as Roman baths in the early fourth century, this red-brick rotunda is the oldest building still standing in Sofia, later folded into a church inside ancient Serdica's walls. Frescoes hide under its dome, the earliest from the tenth century — painted over under Ottoman rule and only uncovered again in the twentieth century.
s: Sofia's oldest building, Roman baths turned church
_facts: Built as Roman baths in the early 4th century CE
Considered the oldest building in modern Sofia
Three layers of frescoes discovered, earliest dating from the 10th century, including 22 prophets over 2m tall
Used as a mosque during the Ottoman era; frescoes uncovered and restored in the 20th century

w: A Czech dynasty built Sofia's two grand river bridges — Václav Prošek, his brother Jozef, and cousins Bohdan and Jiří raised this one over the Vladaya River between 1889 and 1891, linking the new Central Station to the city centre and marking its northern edge ever since.
s: Czech-built 1891 bridge into the city centre
_facts: Built 1889-1891 by Czech architect Václav Prošek with his brother Jozef and cousins Bohdan and Jiří
Gives its name to the junction connecting Central Railway Station with the city centre
Marks the northern border of central Sofia

w: Opened in 1981 to mark 1,300 years of the Bulgarian state, this congress centre was pushed through by Lyudmila Zhivkova, daughter of communist leader Todor Zhivkov. Murals, mosaics and metalwork by Bulgarian artists coat its dark-toned halls — work that won it the title of world's best congress centre in 2005.
s: Communist-era palace, once world's best congress hall
_facts: Opened 31 March 1981 to celebrate the 1300th anniversary of the Bulgarian state
Initiated at the suggestion of Lyudmila Zhivkova, daughter of Todor Zhivkov
Interior features murals, mosaics, sculptures, woodcarvings and metalwork by Bulgarian artists
Proclaimed best congress centre in the world for 2005 by the International Association of Congress Centres

w: Four bronze eagles guard this bridge over the Perlovska River, built in 1891 by the same Czech family who raised the Lions' Bridge two years before. One of its eagle-topped columns appears on the Bulgarian 20-lev banknote, and the square around it has long drawn protesters, notably the 2012 ecological demonstrations.
s: Bronze eagles on a protest-magnet bridge
_facts: Built 1891 by Czech architect Václav Prošek, his brother Jozef and cousins Bohdan and Jiří
Named for four eagle statues on the bridge
One of its columns and bronze eagles appear on the Bulgarian 20 lev banknote (1999, 2007 issues)
The square has been a frequent site of protests, notably the 2012 ecological protests

w: Allied bombs levelled the original cathedral here during the Second World War. Its replacement rose on the same spot with the foundation stone laid personally by Pope John Paul II on his 2002 visit to Bulgaria, and the finished building was inaugurated in 2006 before the Vatican's Cardinal Secretary of State.
s: Rebuilt cathedral, foundation stone laid by a pope
_facts: Destroyed by Allied bombing raids during WWII, rebuilt at the same location
Foundation stone laid personally by Pope John Paul II during his 2002 visit to Bulgaria
Inaugurated 21 May 2006 in the presence of Cardinal Secretary of State Angelo Sodano
Co-cathedral of the Latin Diocese of Sofia and Plovdiv

w: While the Royal Palace downtown handled ceremony and Euxinograd on the coast served as the summer retreat, Vrana was where Bulgaria's royal family actually lived. It remains the official residence of the former royal house, standing on the grounds of the old Chardakli farm, whose bridge featured in the liberation of Sofia.
s: Where Bulgaria's royal family actually lived
_facts: Today the official residence of the former royal family of Bulgaria
Where the royal family spent most of their time, unlike the ceremonial Royal Palace or summer Euxinograd Palace
Situated at an elevation of 571 metres, on the outskirts of Sofia
Includes the site of Chardakli farm, whose bridge featured in the liberation of Sofia

w: Founded by royal decree in 1888, this is the oldest and largest zoological garden in southeastern Europe — 36 hectares that once held nearly 5,000 animals across 840 species. Numbers have thinned since, but several thousand creatures across hundreds of species still call its grounds home today.
s: SE Europe's oldest zoo, founded by royal decree
_facts: Founded by royal decree on 1 May 1888
Oldest and largest zoological garden in Southeast Europe
Covers 36 hectares; housed 4,850 animals across 840 species in 2006
Today hosts around 2,000 animals from 280 species

w: Bulgaria's military history museum has existed in one form or another since 1914, its collection now sprawling across 5,000 square metres indoors and a full 40,000 square metres of outdoor ground — room enough for the tanks and artillery that never fit inside.
s: Tanks and artillery, indoors and out, since 1914
_facts: Existed under various names since 1 August 1914 (in practice since 1916)
A structure of the Ministry of Defence
5,000 sq m of indoor exhibition space plus 40,000 sq m outdoors
Includes a library and computer centre
